title: The Last Inheritance Revisited
premise: When estate lawyer Freya Vasquez is handed a will naming a dead man as beneficiary, he dismisses it as a clerical error — until the testator turns up murdered, dressed in clothes stolen from Freya's own closet. Digging into the town's sealed probate records, Freya discovers that twenty years ago his mentor falsified an inheritance to cover up a death, and the 'closed' case everyone swore was settled was never closed at all. As the killer closes in on everyone who touched those files, Freya realizes the found family he built among the town's outsiders holds both the motive and the key to ending it. In the end, Freya must choose between protecting the town's comfortable lies and exposing the truth, burning the corrupt inheritance to ashes and finding that family, not blood or money, is what's actually passed down.
about_author: Emrys Villalobos is a former small-town court clerk who spent a decade transcribing probate disputes before turning them into fiction. They write mysteries about paper trails, quiet towns, and the people who keep other people's secrets.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Freya Vasquez, POV. Freya reads a newly surfaced will naming a man who died twenty years ago, signed by a testator no one can find. His mentor, Judge Aldous Crane, tells him to shred it. The beat is unease: the first crack in twenty years of alphabetized order.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. The missing testator is found dead in the courthouse annex, wearing a suit stolen from Freya's own closet, with Freya's spare key in its pocket. Detective Imani Okafor names him a person of interest. The beat is panic — the file keeper has become the file.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Alphabetized Silence
chapters.summary: Freya, POV, with flashbacks. Searching sealed probate records, Freya finds the 2004 estate of Daniel Reyes — the dead beneficiary — settled by Crane with signatures Freya doesn't remember witnessing but that bear his name. The beat is vertigo: his own past has been edited.

chapters.title: The Wednesday Supper Club
chapters.summary: Imani Okafor, POV. Imani interviews the members of Freya's weekly supper club — a retired stenographer, a diner cook, a teenage archive volunteer — and finds they all alibi each other too perfectly. The beat is suspicion: even found families have locked doors.

chapters.title: What Daniel Reyes Left Behind
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Freya tracks down Reyes's daughter, Marisol, who reveals her father discovered Crane had diverted town trust funds through fake estates — and died asking questions. The beat is grief hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Shredded, But Not Gone
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Someone ransacks Freya's office; the original will is gone, but the teen volunteer, Priya, secretly digitized it. Crane warns Freya off, invoking the secret they've shared for two decades. The beat is dread — the mentor may be the architect.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Imani, POV. Imani discovers the 2004 witness signature belongs to a woman who left town the week Reyes died — and whose car was pulled from the reservoir last spring. The beat is cold horror: the conspiracy buried more than paperwork.

chapters.title: Confession at the Reservoir
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Confronted at the reservoir, Crane admits falsifying records to hide Reyes's accidental death during a confrontation over the trust funds — but insists someone else is using his old scheme now, killing to keep it buried. The beat is betrayal curdling into alliance.

chapters.title: The Last Filing
chapters.summary: Freya and Imani, alternating POV. The killer — the town clerk who laundered the funds and stole Freya's clothes to frame him — lures Freya to the records vault to destroy the final ledger. Priya's backup copy and the supper club's intervention turn the trap around. The beat is the climax: paper versus blood, and paper wins.

chapters.title: Probate Closed
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Months later, the trust is restored to Marisol, Crane faces sentencing, and Freya testifies to his own complicity in the silence. At the Wednesday supper, now including Marisol and Priya, he files one last document: his resignation from keeping secrets. The beat is resolution — inheritance redefined as what we choose to carry together.
